title: B2+ · L43 — Tech vocabulary (advanced)
description: Vocabulario tecnico avanzado: infrastructure, scalability, latency, throughput, y architecture patterns.

questions.prompt: En un post-mortem de infra un SRE explica el problema.
questions.question: 'Latency' in tech refers to:
options: Total available memory in a system.
The time delay between a request and its response.
The percentage of time a system is running.
questions.explanation: Latency = tiempo entre que envias un request y recibes la respuesta. Distinta de 'bandwidth' (cantidad de datos por segundo). Critica para gaming, trading (HFT), video conferencing, y cualquier real-time. Medida en milliseconds (ms) o microseconds (µs). Registro: senior engineering. Metricas comunes: p50 (mediana), p95, p99 (peor 1% de requests) — 'tail latency' importa mas que la media. Regla practica: usuarios notan latencia >100ms; >1s es percibida como bug. Error hispano frecuente: pronunciar 'latency' /ˈleɪtənsi/ — no 'la-TEN-cy'.
examples: Users start noticing latency above 100ms — it feels sluggish. → threshold conocido
We optimized the API to bring p99 latency below 200ms even under peak load. → engineering goal

questions.prompt: Investor pregunta si el sistema aguantara 100x el trafico actual.
questions.question: 'Scalability' means:
options: The ability of a system to handle increased load without breaking.
The visual design of the interface.
questions.explanation: Scalability = capacidad de un sistema para manejar aumentos de carga (users, requests, data) sin degradarse. Dos estrategias: vertical scaling ('scale up' = maquina mas potente, tiene techo) y horizontal scaling ('scale out' = mas maquinas, casi ilimitado si el sistema es stateless). Central en cloud architecture. Registro: senior engineering. Familia: 'scalable' (adjetivo), 'scale' (verbo — 'this doesn't scale'), 'scalability wall' (limite estructural). Error hispano frecuente: escribir 'escalability' o 'scalability' con 'e' inicial — es 'scalability' /ˌskeɪləˈbɪləti/.
examples: The system scales horizontally to millions of concurrent users without re-architecting. → arquitectura cloud
Scalability was baked in from day one — no last-minute rewrites needed. → decision de diseno

questions.statement: 'Throughput' measures how much data or work a system can process per unit of time.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Throughput = trabajo procesado por unidad de tiempo (requests/sec, GB/hour, transactions/minute). DISTINTA de latency (tiempo por request individual). Ambos importan y a veces hay trade-off: puedes optimizar throughput agrupando (batching) pero eso aumenta latency por request. Registro: senior engineering. Metricas relacionadas: RPS (requests per second), QPS (queries per second), IOPS (input/output operations per second). Error hispano: confundir throughput con bandwidth — bandwidth es capacidad TEORICA del canal, throughput es lo que REALMENTE se logra procesar. Familia: 'peak throughput', 'sustained throughput', 'throughput bottleneck'.
examples: The database sustains fifty thousand writes per second under normal load. → benchmark de infra
Throughput dropped by 30% after the schema change — we're investigating the cause. → incident report

questions.prompt: En un SLA con cliente enterprise se negocia la disponibilidad.
questions.question: 'Uptime' refers to:
options: The percentage of time a system is operational and available.
The speed at which code compiles.
questions.explanation: Uptime = porcentaje del tiempo que el sistema esta operativo y accesible. Se mide en 'nines': 'three nines' = 99.9% (~8.8h downtime/ano), 'four nines' = 99.99% (~52 min/ano), 'five nines' = 99.999% (~5 min/ano). SLA standard en enterprise contracts. Registro: senior infra / SRE. Familia: 'downtime' (opuesto), 'SLA' (Service Level Agreement — promesa), 'SLO' (objective — meta interna), 'SLI' (indicator — metrica), 'error budget' (cuanto downtime toleras dentro del SLA). Error hispano: pensar que 100% uptime es posible — no lo es a escala; siempre hay una probabilidad de fallo.
examples: Our SLA guarantees 99.9% uptime — 'three nines' in industry jargon. → contrato tipico
Any downtime below the SLA triggers service credits on the customer's next invoice. → mecanismo comercial

questions.text: The service is designed to be highly available with automatic failover and zero downtime deployments.
questions.explanation: Frase de senior engineering / architect. 'Highly available' (HA — colocacion), 'automatic failover' (cuando falla una instancia, el trafico se redirige automaticamente a otra), 'zero downtime deployments' (poder actualizar codigo sin interrumpir servicio, via blue-green o rolling deploys). Feature de connected speech: 'highly available' /ˈhaɪli əˈveɪləbl/ — la /i/ final de 'highly' se enlaza con la vocal de 'available'; 'zero downtime' /ˈzɪəroʊ ˈdaʊntaɪm/. Registro: infrastructure engineering. Colocaciones core del vocabulario cloud-native.
examples: HA setup with active-active failover across three regions — zero single points of failure. → arquitectura resiliente
We ship zero-downtime deploys twice a day — no user ever sees a maintenance page. → practica moderna

questions.prompt: Un CTO explica la arquitectura tras migrar del monolito.
questions.question: 'Microservices' architecture means:
options: Small utility functions inside one big application.
An application split into small, independently-deployable services.
Small applications only for mobile devices.
questions.explanation: Microservices = arquitectura donde la aplicacion se compone de servicios pequenos, independientes, cada uno con su propio deploy, su base de datos, y a menudo su equipo. Trade-off vs monolith: mas independencia y velocidad de deploy por equipo, PERO mucha mas complejidad operacional (networking, observability, distributed tracing, versionado de APIs). NO siempre es la respuesta correcta — para startups pequenas suele ser overkill. Registro: senior engineering / architecture. Familia: 'monolith' (opuesto), 'service mesh', 'API gateway', 'domain-driven design'. Error hispano: escribir 'micro services' separado — el standard es 'microservices' junto.
examples: We migrated from monolith to microservices last year — huge undertaking, mixed results. → experiencia comun
Microservices add operational overhead — only worth it once you actually need the scale. → matiz senior

questions.prompt: Empareja cada termino de infrastructure con su equivalente en espanol:
questions.explanation: Vocabulario indispensable de infrastructure moderna. 'Redundancy' = duplicacion intencional para tolerar fallos (multiple availability zones, multiple regions, multiple providers). 'Load balancer' = componente que distribuye trafico entre backend servers segun estrategias (round-robin, least-connections, weighted). Registro: senior engineering. Familia: 'active-active' (todas las replicas atienden trafico), 'active-passive' (solo una atiende, otra en standby). Error hispano: 'balancer' se pronuncia /ˈbælənsər/ — con acento en 'BAL', no en 'CER'.
examples: Redundancy across three availability zones — one can fail and users see nothing. → resilience
The load balancer routes traffic based on real-time health checks. → mecanismo tecnico

questions.target: We hit a scaling wall at 10K RPS, so we sharded the database and added read replicas to handle the load.
questions.explanation: Discurso senior engineering — story tipica en post-mortem o architecture review. 'Scaling wall' (limite estructural que fuerza rearquitectura), 'RPS' (requests per second — jerga standard), 'sharded database' (particionamos la BD por clave), 'read replicas' (copias solo-lectura para offloadear queries). Ritmo natural: pausa breve tras 'RPS,', enfasis tonico en 'sharded' y 'read replicas'. Contracciones no aplican en registro tecnico serio. Registro: senior engineering / architecture review. Estructura clasica: problema tecnico + solucion arquitectonica.
examples: We hit the ceiling at 50K QPS, so we introduced Redis caching in front of Postgres. → solucion tipica
Latency spiked; we added CDN caching to offload origin — solved within a week. → incident resolution

questions.prompt: Un frontend engineer explica el stack de performance.
questions.question: 'CDN' stands for:
questions.explanation: CDN = Content Delivery Network. Red de servidores geo-distribuidos que sirven contenido estatico (imagenes, JS, CSS, videos) desde el POP (point of presence) mas cercano al usuario. Reduce latencia significativamente y offloadea trafico del origin server. Proveedores: Cloudflare, Akamai, Fastly, AWS CloudFront. Registro: engineering. Familia: 'edge computing' (llevar computacion cerca del usuario, no solo contenido), 'cache invalidation' (uno de los dos hardest problems in CS segun el chiste), 'TTL' (time-to-live — cuanto tiempo se cachea). Error hispano: decir 'una CDN' en spanish suena bien; en anglo se dice 'a CDN' o 'the CDN'.
examples: The CDN cuts image load times by 70% in Latin America. → mejora medida
We put all static assets behind a CDN — origin servers barely see traffic now. → arquitectura estandar

questions.statement: 'Tech debt' refers to the future cost of choosing quick, suboptimal solutions today to ship faster.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Tech debt (technical debt) = deuda tecnica. Metafora financiera acunada por Ward Cunningham: como una deuda, el interes se acumula (mas dificil de cambiar el codigo, mas bugs, mas frustacion). Central en engineering culture. NO toda tech debt es mala — 'shipping fast now, refactoring later' es a veces la decision correcta. La pregunta es: te lo pagas conscientemente y con plan de repago, o se te acumula silenciosamente hasta paralizarte? Registro: engineering. Familia: 'debt sprint' (sprint dedicado a pagar debt), 'refactor', 'legacy code', 'greenfield' (proyecto nuevo, sin debt).
examples: We're drowning in tech debt from the early years — every feature takes twice as long as it should. → dolor senior
Some tech debt is fine — you can't be perfect. The question is whether you're managing it. → matiz maduro

questions.prompt: Onboarding de un dev jr, se explica un acronimo omnipresente.
questions.question: 'API' means:
questions.explanation: API = Application Programming Interface. Contract entre dos sistemas software para comunicarse: qué endpoints existen, qué datos aceptan, qué devuelven, qué errores pueden lanzar. Central en toda tech moderna. Tipos comunes: REST (mas usado, sobre HTTP + JSON), GraphQL (mas flexible en consulta, cliente pide lo que necesita), gRPC (binario, rapido, popular en microservices internos), SOAP (legacy, XML). Registro: engineering. Familia: 'endpoint' (URL concreta), 'rate limit' (max requests/min), 'API key' (auth token), 'API versioning' (v1, v2 para no romper clients). Error hispano: usar 'una API' en spanish oral pero escribir siempre 'API' en singular o plural con 's' segun contexto.
examples: We expose a REST API for third-party integrations — well documented, versioned. → producto tecnico
The API is versioned to prevent breaking existing clients when we ship changes. → best practice

questions.text: The rollout was gated behind a feature flag so we could enable it gradually across cohorts.
questions.explanation: Discurso engineering moderno. 'Gated behind a feature flag' (controlado por un toggle que decide quien ve el feature) — practica deploy-safety estandar. 'Enable it gradually across cohorts' (rollout progresivo: 1% de users, luego 5%, luego 25%...) para detectar bugs sin exponer a toda la base. Feature de connected speech: 'gated behind' /ˈɡeɪtɪd bɪˈhaɪnd/ — la /d/ final se pega a la /b/; 'feature flag' /ˈfiːtʃər flæɡ/ con enlazado suave. Registro: senior engineering. Familia: LaunchDarkly y Split.io son plataformas de feature flags populares. 'Ring-based deployment' (rings: dogfood → beta → GA).
examples: We shipped it behind a flag and turned it on for one percent of traffic first. → practica canary
Feature flags let us decouple deploy from release — a game-changer for velocity and safety. → paradigma moderno

questions.prompt: En una entrevista tecnica te preguntan que orquestador usas.
questions.question: 'Kubernetes' is:
questions.explanation: Kubernetes (K8s) = orquestador de containers open-source, creado por Google (basado en Borg interno) y donado a la CNCF. Automatiza deployment, scaling, networking, self-healing de aplicaciones containerizadas. Standard de facto en cloud-native infrastructure. Registro: senior infra / DevOps. Familia: 'container' (unidad de packaging, Docker es el estandar), 'pod' (unidad basica de K8s, contiene uno o mas containers), 'namespace' (aislamiento logico), 'ingress' (gateway HTTP), 'operator' (extension custom). CUIDADO: K8s es POTENTE pero COMPLEJO — muchas startups pequenas se van a K8s cuando bastaba con algo mas simple (Fly.io, Render, Vercel, ECS).
examples: We run everything on Kubernetes — great for scale, painful to operate. → matiz honesto
K8s adds complexity — not always the right choice for a five-person team. → advertencia senior

questions.statement: 'Zero-trust' security assumes no user or system is trusted by default, even inside the corporate network.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Zero-trust = paradigma de seguridad 'never trust, always verify'. OPUESTO al modelo tradicional del castle-and-moat (firewall externo + confiar en todo lo interno). Motivacion: los ataques modernos entran via credenciales robadas, phishing, dispositivos personales — el perimetro clasico ya no existe con cloud + remote work. Estandar moderno en enterprise security. Registro: senior security. Familia: 'BeyondCorp' (implementacion pionera de Google), 'mTLS' (autenticacion mutua), 'least privilege' (dar solo los permisos minimos necesarios), 'micro-segmentation'. Error hispano: escribir 'zero trust' sin guion en contexto tecnico — el standard es 'zero-trust' con guion cuando es adjetivo.
examples: We moved to a zero-trust architecture last year — every request authenticates and authorizes. → migracion moderna
Zero-trust means every request is authenticated and authorized, regardless of origin network. → definicion operativa

questions.target: The system is fully cloud-native, container-based, and horizontally scalable — but the operational complexity is significant.
questions.explanation: Discurso senior architect en design review. Tricolon tecnico ('cloud-native', 'container-based', 'horizontally scalable') seguido de un HEDGE honesto que reconoce el trade-off ('operational complexity is significant'). Marca de arquitecto maduro: no oculta los costes. Ritmo natural: cadencia rapida en el tricolon, pausa reflexiva antes del 'but', tono descendente y grave en 'significant'. Contracciones no aplican en registro architecture review. Registro: senior engineering / architecture review. Formula transferible: describir la arquitectura + reconocer el trade-off principal.
examples: We're serverless-first, event-driven, with eventual consistency — trades latency spikes for scalability. → resumen sofisticado
Multi-region, active-active, with automated failover — resilient but complex to debug when things go wrong. → matiz honesto
